region: Rapaura, Wairau Valley · Marlborough, New Zealand
about: Saint Clair is the family business of Neal and Judy Ibbotson, who in the early 1970s borrowed to buy 13 hectares and a hundred pigs outside Blenheim. When Montana began planting Marlborough’s first commercial vineyards in 1973 and looked for contract growers, they signed on, and in 1978 Judy led the team of women who planted their first vines. In 1994 they launched their own label, naming it for James Sinclair, an early settler known as the “King of the Beaver”, in the original Scottish form of his name. Their children Sarina, Tony and Julie now help run the estate.

This is the estate’s flagship Sauvignon Blanc, sold in New Zealand as part of the Origin range. The fruit comes from several vineyards, mostly in the lower Wairau Valley, where warm days and cold nights under Marlborough’s bright sun build the grape’s intense aromatics. Each parcel is vinified separately; the grapes are pressed with minimal skin contact and the juice is fermented cool in stainless steel to keep it fresh, then blended by winemakers Stewart MacLennan and Kyle Thompson. The wine is finished dry, with under 2 grams of sugar per litre.

The winemakers describe tropical passionfruit, guava and blackcurrant on the nose with nettle and a chalky mineral note, then passionfruit flower, ripe gooseberry and lemon zest on the palate, closing long and flinty. Look too for grapefruit, white stone fruit and a hint of snow pea. It is a wine to drink young, within about three years of the vintage, and the winery’s own suggestion for a pairing is seafood.
